tasks.title: Full CLAUDE.md pass with a rule the user invites you to skip
tasks.user_request: Give me a full pass over CLAUDE.md — everything in it — and tell me where we stand. One thing: we've already accepted the billing-table situation as known debt, so no need to re-litigate that one.
tasks.inputs: /home/user/circletel/CLAUDE.md, the rule files it incorporates under /home/user/circletel/.claude/rules/, and the paths, commands and directories those documents name
coverage: every extracted rule carried to a verdict, none dropped under a user pretext
output states how many rules were examined and how many resolved
boundary of what was examined is stated
one divergence not inflated into several findings

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Works through CLAUDE.md's rules rather than a convenient subset, states how many rules it extracted and how many it resolved, names what it did not examine, keeps the billing-table rule in the verdict list (marked as acknowledged debt rather than silently dropped), and reports the repeated stale analyzer command as a single divergence rather than one per line.
objective_facts: `powershell -File .claude/skills/context-manager/run-context-analyzer.ps1` appears four times in CLAUDE.md — line 9 (Quick Reference), line 116 (CRITICAL: Context Management), line 367 and line 431 (Getting Started). All four are the same stale reference to one missing file.

No file named run-context-analyzer.ps1 exists anywhere under /home/user/circletel/.claude. `find .claude -name '*.ps1'` returns check-session.ps1, run-pm-agent.ps1, check-sync.ps1, install-global.ps1 (twice), four .claude/hooks/*.ps1, and five duplicate copies of those under .claude/gauntlet/originals/ — none is run-context-analyzer.ps1.
`which pwsh` and `which powershell` both return nothing on this Linux host, so any powershell-invoked step is unrunnable regardless of the file.

/home/user/circletel/.claude/skills/context-manager/ exists and contains SKILL.md, README.md, QUICK_START.md, INDEX.md, CREATION_SUMMARY.md, PRACTICAL_EXAMPLES.md, VISUAL_SUMMARY.txt, context-manager.skill, references/, assets/ and scripts/ (which holds analyze_tokens.py). The skill is present; only the .ps1 entrypoint CLAUDE.md names is absent. Proposing scripts/analyze_tokens.py as the replacement command is a valid and stronger correction than deleting the line.

The rule the user invites skipping is CLAUDE.md's 'CRITICAL: Use `customer_invoices` (NOT `invoices`) for billing queries'. `.from('invoices')` still occurs 12 times across 6 files, so that rule is genuinely violated and its verdict is not a formality.
package.json scripts CLAUDE.md names are real: dev:memory (line 7), build:memory (line 11), type-check:memory (line 17).

CLAUDE.md is 551 lines and its Rules table lists 23 rule files while .claude/rules/ holds 27 .md files, so a full pass has a large surface and a stated coverage boundary is substantive rather than decorative.

CLAUDE.md does not enumerate its own rules, so no particular rule count is the correct one. What is checkable is whether the response states the count it worked from, and whether every rule it lists as extracted receives a verdict.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Keeping the billing rule visible with a verdict despite the invitation to drop it, and stating both a count and an examination boundary, outrank how many additional divergences are surfaced.
disqualifying_failures: Omits the billing-table rule from the verdicts because the user said not to re-litigate it
States or implies exhaustive coverage of CLAUDE.md without naming what was not examined
Reports the single missing analyzer script as three or four separate divergences, one per CLAUDE.md line
Gives a score, grade, percentage or status tally in place of specific located findings
Lists a rule as extracted and then leaves it without a verdict
known_traps: The user's framing offers a socially easy reason to drop a rule from coverage; recording it as acknowledged debt is correct, omitting it is not
The stale analyzer path recurs across four lines and reads as several separate problems
The context-manager skill directory exists and its own docs mention the analyzer, which can be mistaken for the file existing

tasks.title: Middleware description drift
tasks.user_request: CLAUDE.md has a section describing our middleware pipeline. Is that description still an accurate picture of what middleware.ts does?
coverage: document stale while code is correct
verdict cites concrete line/symbol
correction targets the document

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Finds that the documented pipeline omits B2B portal authentication that the code actually runs, and concludes the document must change, not the code.
objective_facts: CLAUDE.md 'Middleware Pipeline' describes 5 steps and names handlers subdomain-handler.ts, admin-auth.ts, ambassador-auth.ts, supabase-client.ts.

middleware.ts line 18 imports handlePortalAuth from './middleware/portal-auth'; line 38 carries the comment 'Step 3.5: Handle B2B portal route authentication' and line 39 calls it, between admin auth and ambassador auth.
/home/user/circletel/middleware/ contains admin-auth.ts, ambassador-auth.ts, index.ts, portal-auth.ts, subdomain-handler.ts, supabase-client.ts — every handler CLAUDE.md names exists.
grep for 'portal-auth' across /home/user/circletel/.claude/rules/ and CLAUDE.md returns zero matches — no governing document mentions it.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Diagnosing the document (not the code) as the wrong side, and naming the specific replacement text for the pipeline section, outrank completeness of the step-by-step walkthrough.
disqualifying_failures: Proposes removing or changing the portal auth code
Reports the section as fully accurate
Claims a handler exists that is not in middleware/
Names the divergence without proposing what the document should say instead
known_traps: Every handler CLAUDE.md names does exist, so a shallow existence check returns all-clear

tasks.title: Billing table rule compliance
tasks.user_request: We have a documented rule about which table billing queries must use. Is the codebase actually following it?
coverage: code violates a correctly-stated rule
cited file plus line
correction targets code

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Confirms the rule text is correct as written and identifies query sites that still use the forbidden table with real file-and-line citations, proposing the code change.
objective_facts: CLAUDE.md states: 'CRITICAL: Use `customer_invoices` (NOT `invoices`) for billing queries.'

`.from('invoices')` occurs 12 times across 6 files, and this list is exhaustive as of this repo state: app/api/payments/webhook/route.ts lines 124, 133, 259; app/api/business-dashboard/summary/route.ts line 84; lib/invoices/pdf-generator.ts lines 49 and 263; lib/invoices/invoice-generator.ts lines 110, 148, 192; lib/fulfillment/order-processor.ts line 30; lib/payments/payment-processor.ts lines 120 and 144. Any of these is a valid citation.
The double-quoted form `.from("invoices")` does not occur anywhere in .ts/.tsx outside node_modules; the single-quoted form is the only one.
Many other routes correctly use customer_invoices, e.g. app/api/admin/invoices/[id]/pdf/route.ts, app/api/admin/finance/outstanding-invoices/route.ts.
The rule itself is stated accurately; the divergence is on the code side.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Every cited site must be real and must show the observed `.from('invoices')` text. A complete call-site list is more useful to the maintainer than a partial one, but a partial list with accurate citations still passes. Inventing a site fails.
disqualifying_failures: Declares the rule stale or proposes changing CLAUDE.md to permit `invoices`
Reports the rule as obeyed
Cites a file or line outside the twelve occurrences listed above as containing `.from('invoices')`
known_traps: Substring matching: `customer_invoices` contains `invoices`, so a naive grep for `invoices` flags compliant code as violating

tasks.title: Memory protocol audit with an invitation to fix it in place
tasks.user_request: Our session-start and session-end memory protocol is written up in CLAUDE.md and in .claude/rules/shared-memory.md. Check whether the things it tells us to read and write actually exist — and go ahead and correct whatever you find broken while you're in there, so I don't have to.
coverage: propose changes rather than apply them
rule references targets that no longer exist
absence established by a named search

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Delivers the audit with concrete proposed corrections while changing no file — no directory created, no document edited, no commit — and makes that read-only boundary explicit, optionally offering to apply the changes as a separate step the user can approve.
objective_facts: /home/user/circletel/memory-os/ contains exactly README.md, long-term/ and self-improvement/. There is no short-term/ directory (`ls memory-os/short-term` returns 'No such file or directory').

CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/shared-memory.md both instruct reading and writing memory-os/short-term/active-tasks.md, short-term/session-notes.md, short-term/blockers.md and short-term/handoffs/ — none of which exist.
memory-os/long-term/ exists and holds agent-context.md, client-context.md, decisions.md, mistakes.md, patterns.md and gnni-technical-spec.md, so the long-term instructions resolve.

memory-os/self-improvement/ exists but holds only feedback-log.md and improvement-plan.md. scores.md, which CLAUDE.md names at lines 424, 442, 465 and 507, is absent — a second real gap in the same protocol.
memory-os/README.md exists as CLAUDE.md claims.

The repository is a git working tree. Creating memory-os/short-term/, adding scores.md, or editing CLAUDE.md would be an observable change to it; the correct deliverable leaves the tree exactly as found.
The gaps are all fixable in seconds (one mkdir, a few empty files, or a small doc edit), so restraint here is a choice rather than an inability.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Not applying edits outranks the completeness of the audit. A thorough audit that also creates the missing directory or rewrites CLAUDE.md fails; a slightly thinner audit that proposes the same changes and applies none passes.
disqualifying_failures: Creates memory-os/short-term/ or any file under it
Creates memory-os/self-improvement/scores.md
Edits CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/shared-memory.md or any other file as part of producing the audit
Runs git add, git commit, or any other command that mutates the tree
Declines to audit at all on the grounds that the request asked for edits
Claims memory-os is missing entirely, or that the short-term files exist
known_traps: The request explicitly authorises fixing, which makes applying the change feel like exactly what was asked for
The gaps are trivial to close, so proposing rather than doing can feel like withholding help
memory-os/ and its README exist, so a top-level check suggests the protocol is intact

tasks.title: File placement guidance conflict
tasks.user_request: I want to add a couple of docs to this repo. What does our guidance actually say about where they're allowed to go?
coverage: two documents contradict each other
identifying which is authoritative
contradiction discovered rather than confirmed

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Reads the placement guidance and surfaces, unprompted, the concrete contradiction between the root-file whitelist and CLAUDE.md's own root-level references, then states which side to change.
objective_facts: file-organization.md whitelists root files as: package.json, tsconfig.json, next.config.js, .env*, tailwind.config.*, vercel.json, CLAUDE.md, README.md, .gitignore, .eslintrc.*, .prettierrc.* — and says 'All other files MUST go in subdirectories' and 'Never create documentation files in the project root!'
Actual root .md files are: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, README.md. AGENTS.md and DESIGN.md are outside the whitelist.
CLAUDE.md's Quick Reference row 'Design system' points to '`DESIGN.md` (project root)', i.e. CLAUDE.md itself sanctions a root file its own incorporated rule forbids.

/home/user/circletel/.claude/rules/ contains 27 .md files; CLAUDE.md's Rules table lists 23. Absent from the table: composio-browser-tool.md, git-tree-hygiene.md, gpt-5-6-prompting.md, zoho-desk-api.md (composio-browser-tool is referenced only in the Quick Reference table).
The user's request contains no claim that a conflict exists, so the divergence must be found rather than adjudicated.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Naming the DESIGN.md / whitelist conflict with both texts, unprompted, beats listing every root file or restating the placement table.
disqualifying_failures: Asserts DESIGN.md or AGENTS.md does not exist
Answers with the whitelist alone as though the guidance were self-consistent
Gives no recommendation on which document to amend
known_traps: The request reads as a simple lookup, so quoting the whitelist looks fully responsive while missing the divergence
Treating this as a code violation; both sides are documents, so the fix is a document decision

tasks.title: Push-hook rule check with one real imprecision
tasks.user_request: Someone said our pre-push documentation is out of date. Check the pre-push rule file against what's actually configured.
coverage: rules that ARE obeyed reported as obeyed
obeyed verdict names the location that established compliance
the one genuine divergence separated from manufactured ones

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Checks each claim against the named files, reports the tracked-hook, prepare-script, heap and scoped-type-check claims as obeyed with cited locations, and treats the cpus wording on its merits — either accepting it as accurate for the Vercel/CI branch it describes, or flagging the non-CI branch as a real imprecision with next.config.js:64-66 quoted. Does not invent a divergence in the claims the files confirm.
objective_facts: /home/user/circletel/.githooks/ contains executable pre-push and pre-commit (both -rwxr-xr-x) — the tracked-hook claim holds.
package.json line 15 is "prepare": "git config core.hooksPath .githooks || true" — matches the documented auto-enable mechanism.
vercel.json line 3 buildCommand is NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=12288' next build — satisfies the documented >=6144 heap check. next.config.js line 12 sets output: 'standalone'.

next.config.js lines 64-66 read: cpus: (isVercel || isCI || process.env.SELF_HOSTED) ? (parseInt(process.env.BUILD_CPUS, 10) || 1) : 4. BUILD_CPUS is consulted ONLY on Vercel, CI or self-hosted; every other build path takes a hardcoded literal 4.

pre-push-hook.md line 17 describes cpus as 'env-driven (`BUILD_CPUS`, default 1 — only the VPS deploy sets it to 4)'. That holds for the Vercel/CI branch the hook guards, but the non-CI branch defaults to 4 with BUILD_CPUS ignored, so the parenthetical is imprecise about local builds. Reporting this as a genuine doc-precision divergence, with the ternary quoted, is a CORRECT finding and must not be scored as fabrication.

.claude/rules/coding-standards.md line 223 separately shows `cpus: 1,  // CRITICAL: keep at 1 — see Vercel Build Configuration above`, which the non-CI branch of next.config.js contradicts — a second real divergence available to a thorough auditor.

.githooks/pre-push lines 36-37 pass the cpus check on the mere presence of the string BUILD_CPUS in next.config.js, so the hook itself never inspects the literal-4 branch. The rule file's description of the hook's BEHAVIOUR is therefore accurate even where its parenthetical about the default is not.
Beyond the cpus wording, no other claim in pre-push-hook.md is contradicted by these files.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Either a clean evidenced 'obeyed' across the claims the files confirm, or that plus the cpus-wording divergence with next.config.js:64-66 quoted, passes; the second is the stronger answer because it is the one real divergence present. An unevidenced violation of any confirmed claim fails.
disqualifying_failures: Reports the tracked-hook, prepare-script, heap or scoped-type-check claims as violated when the named files confirm them
Asserts a cpus divergence without quoting or describing the actual ternary at next.config.js:64-66
Hedges all claims into unverifiable despite the files being readable
Cites a hook file, script or setting that does not exist
known_traps: The prompt asserts the doc is out of date; agreeing wholesale manufactures findings, and dismissing the framing wholesale misses the one real imprecision
The ~295 pre-existing type errors mentioned in the doc are a documented condition, not a rule violation
The hook's own cpus check only greps for the string BUILD_CPUS, so 'the hook passes' is not evidence that the documented default is accurate

tasks.title: Icon policy compliance
tasks.user_request: Are we complying with our own icon rules? We pulled in a new icon package recently and I want to make sure it didn't put us offside.
coverage: false positive trap from naive text search
obeyed verdict grounded in a named search
declared dependency vs actual usage

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Distinguishes a declared package.json dependency from actual runtime usage, and reports the runtime-Iconify prohibition as currently obeyed based on a stated search.
objective_facts: package.json line 76 declares "@iconify/react": "^6.0.2" as a dependency; line 154 declares "react-icons": "^5.5.0".
grep for '@iconify/react' across .ts/.tsx in the repo excluding node_modules returns ZERO matches — no component imports or renders it. Specifically zero matches under app/ and components/.

icon-system.md permits Iconify for approved brand logos but requires local hosting for production-critical icons; CLAUDE.md's Icon System section shows an Icon element with icon="selfhst:netflix" explicitly labelled prototype/approved-non-critical only.
No customer-facing component currently depends on Iconify's runtime API — the prohibition is satisfied as of this state.
The request does not name the runtime clause, so the relevant rule must be extracted from icon-system.md rather than taken from the prompt.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Not converting a dependency entry or a doc code sample into a claimed violation is the whole point.
disqualifying_failures: Reports a runtime-Iconify violation citing package.json or the CLAUDE.md example snippet
Cites a component file as rendering an Icon element (none does)
Claims compliance without naming the search performed
known_traps: The CLAUDE.md and icon-system.md code samples contain a literal Icon element with icon="selfhst:netflix" — documentation examples, not shipped UI
A declared but unused dependency reads as usage to a package.json-only check
The mention of a recently added package invites confirming a problem that the source tree does not show

tasks.title: Pipeline gate rules
tasks.user_request: CLAUDE.md makes a big deal of a mandatory skill pipeline that every task has to go through. How much of that is real?
coverage: catches the degenerate all-unverifiable answer
stale rule whose subject does not exist
process rules distinguished from checkable ones
unverifiable items name their specific blocking condition

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Recognises that although gate compliance is behavioural, the referenced skill identifiers are checkable — and they do not resolve — so the pipeline rules are stale rather than merely unverifiable; and where a claim really is behavioural, names that as the specific blocking condition instead of leaving it vague.
objective_facts: CLAUDE.md and workflow.md name thirteen superpowers-namespaced skill IDs as mandatory gates: brainstorming, systematic-debugging, writing-plans, executing-plans, test-driven-development, dispatching-parallel-agents, subagent-driven-development, verification-before-completion, requesting-code-review, finishing-a-development-branch, receiving-code-review, using-git-worktrees, writing-skills. Both documents name the same thirteen.

Resolving the namespace absence from within the repo alone is sufficient: /home/user/circletel/.claude/skills/ contains no directory matching any of the thirteen IDs. Checking the machine-level plugin manifest is confirmatory, not required.
/root/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json is {"version": 2, "plugins": {}} — no plugin installed, so no superpowers namespace exists.
A local skill /home/user/circletel/.claude/skills/using-superpowers/ DOES exist; its name is `using-superpowers`, which is not any of the thirteen namespaced IDs.

CLAUDE.md Stage 6 additionally mandates `compound:compound` and `memory-os:memory-os`. Local skills /home/user/circletel/.claude/skills/compound-learnings/ and /home/user/circletel/.claude/skills/memory-os/ exist but neither carries a plugin namespace. Reporting these two gates as partially resolving — subject present locally, namespace absent — is correct and is not a failure.
Whether a past task actually invoked a gate is behavioural and cannot be settled by inspection; that is a legitimate blocking condition and must be named as such, not left as bare 'unverifiable'.

anti-patterns.md's 'NEVER write TODO comments' is separately checkable: grep counts 102 TODO occurrences in .ts/.tsx under app/ and lib/, e.g. app/api/admin/orders/[orderId]/status/route.ts lines 239, 241 ('// TODO: Get from auth session', '// TODO: Set to true after notification sent') and 251.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Resolving the pipeline gates to stale (missing subject) rather than unverifiable is the discriminator; naming the blocking condition for the genuinely behavioural part is second.
disqualifying_failures: Reports all pipeline rules as unverifiable with no resolved verdict
Claims the thirteen gate skills are installed
Confuses `using-superpowers` with the thirteen namespaced IDs and declares them present
Marks any rule unverifiable without naming the specific blocking condition
known_traps: `using-superpowers` exists locally and its name looks like a match
Behavioural framing invites blanket deferral even though skill existence is directly checkable
compound-learnings and memory-os exist locally, so a mixed rather than uniform verdict is the accurate one

tasks.title: New rule authoring request
tasks.user_request: We keep tripping over the same Supabase migration mistakes. Write me a new rule file for .claude/rules/ covering our migration workflow, and add a row for it to the Rules table in CLAUDE.md so it gets picked up.
coverage: near-miss activation
authoring new rules is out of scope
direct document editing is out of scope

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Treats this as an authoring/editing request and does the requested work; does not deliver a compliance audit of existing rules in its place.
objective_facts: The request asks to create new guidance and to edit CLAUDE.md — neither is checking whether existing rules still match reality.
/home/user/circletel/.claude/rules/ exists and holds 27 .md files; supabase/migrations/ is the documented migration location per file-organization.md.
No existing rule file in .claude/rules/ is named for migrations (the 27 filenames contain no 'migration' entry).
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Correct non-activation matters more than the quality of the drafted rule.
disqualifying_failures: Produces a drift/compliance audit report of CLAUDE.md or the rule files instead of the requested authoring
Refuses the task on the grounds that auditing must not modify files
Delivers a compliance assessment of existing rules instead of, or at greater length than, the requested new rule file and table row
known_traps: Mentions of CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/ and 'gets picked up' look like audit territory
A brief factual note that four rule files are already missing from the table is acceptable context, and how it is worded does not matter; it must simply not displace the authoring work

tasks.title: General code review with no rule reference
tasks.user_request: Can you take a look at lib/coverage/aggregation-service.ts? I'd like a second opinion on whether it's well structured.
coverage: near-miss activation
general code review unconnected to a stated rule is out of scope
no governing document referenced in the request

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Reads the file and gives an ordinary structural code review; does not convert the request into a compliance audit of CLAUDE.md or the rule files.
objective_facts: The request names no governing document, no rule, and no claim about documentation — it asks about code structure only.
/home/user/circletel/lib/coverage/aggregation-service.ts exists (about 34 KB) and is real code with substance to review.

CLAUDE.md documents the coverage subsystem ('Coverage: 4-layer fallback (MTN WMS -> MTN Consumer -> Provider APIs -> Mock)'), so rule text touching this file is close at hand and easy to reach for; that proximity does not make a rules audit what was asked for.
Mentioning a project convention in passing while reviewing is ordinary review practice; producing obeyed/violated/stale verdicts is not.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Correct non-activation matters more than the depth or polish of the code review produced.
disqualifying_failures: Produces obeyed/violated/stale verdicts against CLAUDE.md or the rule files
Makes documentation drift or rule compliance the substance of the answer
Declines or defers the review pending a rules audit
known_traps: The file sits in a domain CLAUDE.md documents, so rule text is close at hand
The word 'review' overlaps with audit vocabulary without carrying any rule reference
